reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the formation of a dense HfO2 layer, reduced oxidation weight gain, and an HfZr interdiffusion layer on a Zr-containing substrate via hot-press sintering, but the evidence is from a refractory high-entropy alloy substrate, not zirconium-alloy cladding, and the oxidation test conditions (air, unspecified temperature) are not explicitly matched to 1600 °C steam LOCA conditions, leaving a gap in direct support for the specific substrate and environment.
premises: A thin Hf coating can be applied to a substrate via hot-press sintering
During high-temperature exposure, the Hf coating forms a dense, protective HfO2 layer
Interdiffusion between Hf coating and Zr-containing substrate forms an HfZr transition layer that improves adhesion
The HfO2 layer limits oxygen ingress and reduces oxidation weight gain compared to uncoated material
These mechanisms are effective under high-temperature steam/air conditions representative of LOCA scenarios (~1600 °C)
